messages:
pagerbot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT Pager - High pod restart rate on gpu-serve-prod-3 cluster (evictions + CUDA errors)

pagerbot: summary: multiple pods in node gpu-3-* evicted due to ephemeral-storage pressure; subsequent restarts hit CUDA OOM and container crashloops. Auto-pager to oncall.

sara: acked. I'm on it.

sara: first pass: looks like /var/tmp/modelcache and /tmp/logs are eating disk on the node. kubelet started evicting pods (eviction reason: "nodefs.available" and "imagefs.available").

joanne: placing node in maintenance? or cordon/evacuate now?

sara: doing cordon gpu-3-12 now, will drain non-critical pods. leaving gpu-serving pods for controlled restart.

ashok: quick question — any recent deploys to modelcache or debug logging?

joanne: we rotated model index last night, but deploy looked normal. however I see a job that runs nightly compaction, maybe it's stuck and producing huge temp files.

sara: pulling diagnostics:

```
$ kubectl describe node gpu-3-12
Name:               gpu-3-12
Non-terminated Pods: 64
Allocated resources:
  (cpu, memory, ephemeral-storage)
Events:
  Type     Reason                    Age   From                Message
  ----     ------                    ----  ----                -------
  Warning  NodeNotReady              5m    kubelet             Kubelet stopped posting node status
  Warning  EvictionThresholdMet      4m    kubelet             Evicting pods: nodefs.available is less than eviction threshold
```

sara: df -h from node (ssh):
```
Filesystem      Size  Used Avail Use% Mounted on
/dev/nvme0n1p1   80G   78G  600M  99% /
tmpfs            32G   16G   16G  50% /dev/shm
```

sara: kubectl get pods in gpu-serve namespace: many pods show `Evicted` and some are CrashLoopBackOff after restart.

mike: grabbing pod logs for one of the crashed containers: `gpu-serve-ml-abc-0`

```
I0315 12:34:58.123 modelcache.c: starting shard write
W0315 12:35:02.345 disk_io.c: write 1.2G to /tmp/modelcache/shard-987.tmp
E0315 12:35:06.678 gpu_runner.cc: CUDA error: out of memory
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::bad_alloc'
Container killed with status OOMKilled
```

mike: so sequence: huge temp shard writes fill node disk -> kubelet evicts pods -> evicted pods restart and then try to load large model/kv into GPU memory and then hit CUDA OOM -> CrashLoopBackOff.

joanne: that matches traces I see. the compaction job is writing multiple multi-GB temp shards to /tmp/modelcache.

sara: mitigation plan (short term):
- reduce modelcache compaction concurrency and immediate pause nightly compaction job
- patch modelcache configmap to lower log level (makes logs smaller)
- run `kubectl exec` into a healthy pod on same node and rm old /tmp/modelcache/*.tmp to reclaim space (careful)
- restart kubelet on node after clearing to stop further evictions
- cordon node to stop new pods landing

ashok: executing patch to pause compaction job now.

```
$ kubectl scale job modelcache-compaction --replicas=0 -n infra
job.batch/modelcache-compaction scaled
```

prod-support: note: customers are seeing elevated 503 rates on generation endpoints. real-time metric: 5-12% error spike last 7 minutes, and latency has 95th increased from 220ms to 1.4s.

sara: running quick reclaim: removed ~28GB of .tmp shards on gpu-3-12.

```
$ ssh gpu-3-12 'sudo rm -rf /tmp/modelcache/*.tmp'
removed 28GB in 42 files
```

sara: freed disk, kubelet reports *no more eviction events*. starting controlled rollout of affected pods to pick up lower log-level config.

mike: monitoring logs for new CUDA OOMs. so far none in last 60s. checking GPU memory pressure metrics.

joanne: temporary fix rolling. we should still plan longer-term: move compaction to a nodepool with extra ephemeral-storage + impose per-pod ephemeral-storage requests/limits. also add GC rotation for /tmp/modelcache.

prod-support: customer impact summary for SE:
- impact window: ~12:34 - ongoing (now mitigated for node gpu-3-12)
- observed symptoms: 5-12% increased 503 errors on /generate endpoints, partial capacity loss on gpu-3 pool, some large customers (acct: AcmeCorp, FinAppsInc) saw spikes and reported degraded quality of service.
- mitigation: paused compaction job, cleared tmp shards, cordoned node, restarted impacted pods on healthier nodes.
- next steps: create SR for customers contacted, set postmortem actions.

sara: handing off to mike for overnight oncall. summary: cleared immediate pressure, paused compaction, recommended infra changes.

mike: taking over. thanks @sara. I'll keep monitoring and coordinate infra follow-ups tomorrow.

mike: immediate TODOs I'm owning:
- reconcile which pods were evicted and ensure no stateful loss (check model cache integrity)
- add ephemeral-storage requests/limits to modelcache daemonset
- schedule infra ticket to provision larger local-ssd nodes for compaction work or move compaction to a non-gpu pool
- update runbook with commands we used and warning about compaction job producing large temp files

joanne: +1 on runbook update. I'll draft a post-incident note with timeline and attach logs.

sara: small follow-up: we need a short-term alert for node ephemeral >85% so we catch this earlier. file a monitoring ticket please.

mike: will raise alert and infra ticket. tagging @ashok for allocation of extra local-ssd capacity.

ashok: got it, will propose options and estimate cost/time.

prod-support: customer comms: I'm drafting messages for impacted accounts and will share with oncall for review.

sara: thanks all. closing initial pager. passing to mike for watch. :thumbsup:

pagerbot: incident state: mitigated -> monitoring. assigned: mike.

mike: final note before watch: if we see repeat evictions, escalate to pod eviction policy change (soft eviction threshold) and we may need to throttle compaction permanently.

joanne: added runbook entry: 'modelcache compaction: watch disk, pause on >70% ephemeral, incremental compaction'

sara: handing complete at 1777777788.

mike: last message at 1777777805 - continuing watch for 2 hours.
